title: Sephiria Characters — Hero, Costumes & Tower NPCs (1.0)
description: Sephiria characters guide: the playable rabbit hero, how costumes change opening stats, and the village and tower NPCs that gate weapons and secret skins.
meta: Covers sephiria characters / NPC searches; pairs with the costume roster page. One playable hero; six NPC entries, two of which gate unlocks.
body:
Sephiria has one playable hero — the rabbit — plus a roster of costumes that change how a run starts. Everyone else is an NPC, and two of them gate weapon unlocks and a secret costume.

Who you play

You play the rabbit of Bunnyville. There is no class pick and no second hero, so your real character choice is the costume — and costumes are not cosmetic, because each one trades opening stats against each other. That makes them behave like a pre-run loadout rather than a skin.

How costumes change a run

  • Costumes set opening stats and trade-offs, so they shift which build comes online fastest — see builds.
  • Some are unlocked by challenges rather than bought. The costume roster page lists every skin with its effect and unlock condition.
  • Roster size depends on when you count: the launch listing says over 20 costumes, while the community database tracked at v1.0.24 lists 27 playable skins (8 from the start, 19 unlocked).

Non-playable characters

CharacterWhereWhat they do
Moro (written Morrow in some guides)Village training ground, east sideUnlocks weapon branches once you own the matching Destiny Inscription node. Community data lists Greatsword, Dagger, Crossbow, Blade and Staff on this route, with Sword and Shield excluded
Manok, the friendly wandererVillage, at the Iron MaidenRuns the Blood Donation event; donating five times across runs unlocks the Wingless Bat costume
ElruHides in three spots: the carrot farm, the pond by the clothing shop, and the Ark puzzle roomThe Hide and Seek event target, and a repeatable Destiny Inscription event

NPC roles and locations come from community records, including the in-game Destiny Inscription event text. If a village event has moved in a patch, your client wins.

Effects are the community snapshot also published on the costume roster page; the “who it suits” column is our read of the trade, not a game fact. Three of the eight have no effect recorded in the audited source — that gap is printed rather than filled.

Choosing a costume in one sentence

Pick the drawback you can live with, not the bonus you like most. A damage bonus on a run that keeps dying to chip damage loses to a defence trade every time; a defence trade on a run that never gets hit is wasted. Since the costume is chosen before the floor, it is the first build decision of the run — not a cosmetic one.

Which entries matter first

Three kinds of entry share this page and they do different jobs. The hero section decides nothing, because there is one playable rabbit and no class pick. The costume table is the real pre-run choice, because every row trades one opening stat for another. The NPC table is a list of gates: two of those names open content that no amount of play inside a floor will open by itself.

Read them in that order of consequence. A costume changes every floor of the run. Moro changes which weapons exist for you at all. Manok changes one unlock that otherwise needs five separate donations. Elru is a repeatable event rather than a gate, and Hizo, Connor and Valter are listed as village event NPCs and nothing more.

How the costume choice meets the weapon and the Companion build

Costume trades are stat-shaped, so they favour different weapon families. Attack speed and dash recovery on Braided Hair Rabbit suit a family that wants to stay in contact — the weapons page lists Katana as aggressive melee with a steeper mastery curve and Dagger as fast reaction melee with extremely short reach, so both keep you at close range. Brown Rabbit is listed for players who already dodge on reaction rather than block, which is the habit short reach rewards. Defense on Armored Rabbit matches Sword and Shield, which the weapons page lists for first runs and pattern learning.

Orange Rabbit is the one entry the page ties to a damage type rather than a range: debuff damage, for runs already built around burn, freeze or shock. That is a condition, not a bonus you can plan around later in the run — if the build is not already that shape, the +14% has nothing to act on.

The Companion build sits awkwardly against all of this. Its damage comes from pets, so personal attack speed and personal crit buy less there than they do on a melee route; the companion checklist asks instead for a weapon and family chosen before the run, companions stacked on floor one, and Tablets spent on summons rather than on your own DPS. On that route a costume that keeps you upright while the board comes online is doing more work than one that raises your own output, and the carry lines the build leans on come from progression rather than from a costume.

Common mistakes

  • Reading a costume as an upgrade. Every recorded row is a trade. The one that looks free, Pink Bunny, is recorded as free; the rest name what they take.
  • Planning around the three silent costumes. Red-Hooded, White and Wing-Eared appear in the roster with no effect in the audited source. That is a gap, not a hint at something strong.
  • Looking for a class pick. There is one hero, so time spent choosing a class is time not spent choosing a costume or a weapon branch.
  • Walking past Moro. Branches unlock through the training ground once the Destiny node is owned; skipping the NPC leaves the branch locked even with the node paid for.
  • Skipping Manok because the event looks optional. Five donations across runs is the only route to the Wingless Bat costume that this page lists.
  • Treating a roster count as a spending plan. The launch listing says over 20; the community database at v1.0.24 counts 27 playable skins, 8 at the start and 19 unlocked. Both can be true of different moments.
  • Assuming a location is permanent. NPC roles and locations come from community records, so if a village event moved in a patch, your client wins.

What this page leaves to other pages

  • Every costume and its unlock condition — the costume roster page, including the 19 unlockables and the one condition the sources still disagree on.
  • The nodes Moro’s branches depend on — Destiny Inscription, for Sapphire spend order and talent resets.
  • What to do with a branch once it unlocks — weapons and upgrades for the six families and the routes that finish.
  • Matching a costume to a specific plan — builds, and the Companion build for the summoner route.
  • Running the same rabbit with friends — co-op for revives and shared loot, and multiplayer setup for opening a lobby.

Questions this page answers directly

Is there more than one playable character?

No. You play the rabbit of Bunnyville; there is no class pick and no second hero, which is why the costume carries the choice.

Are costumes cosmetic?

Not in the recorded data. Each starting costume sets opening stats and trades them against each other, so the page treats them as a pre-run loadout rather than a skin.

How many costumes are there?

Two counts appear here. The launch listing says over 20, and the community database at v1.0.24 lists 27 playable skins, 8 from the start and 19 unlocked. The full list with effects is on the costume roster page.

Who unlocks new weapon branches?

Moro, at the village training ground on the east side, once you own the matching Destiny Inscription node. The community list of branches on that route covers Greatsword, Dagger, Crossbow, Blade and Staff; Sword and Shield is the one exclusion.

How do I get the Wingless Bat costume?

Donate five times at the Iron Maiden with Manok, across runs. The count is cumulative, not a single session.

Why do three of the eight starting costumes have no effect listed?

Because the audited source does not record one for Red-Hooded, White or Wing-Eared. Check them in your own client before planning a run around them.
